explanations.explanation: It detects formal, document‐style language—that is, texts with structured metadata (dates, case numbers, citations, proper names) and specialized, official tone (legalese, journalistic or scholarly reporting) that signal authoritative, archival or institutional content.

The feature appears to detect and represent boilerplate legal header or license text, particularly those for Apache-licensed software, including copyright notices, version numbers, disclaimer language, and the standard “express or implied” warranty clauses.

It appears that the feature “lights up” on structured, domain‐specific metadata—especially the kinds of citation markers, alphanumeric identifiers, and formatted numeric strings (including dates, file names, and reference codes) typically found in academic or technical texts.
